prompt: A wool hat dries beside the low stove in the quiet room.
Wind pushes a loose branch against the shed while rain fills the path.
A wooden horse faces the other way after the room was empty.
An older child brings two cups and leaves the smaller one for Leo.
Steam fades above the bowl near a clean red towel.
Three buttons lie in a line where only one had been before.
A patient visitor waits while Leo finishes tying his shoe.
Rain strikes the metal step and a cold draft moves the curtain.
Dark clouds cross the yard as water taps every window at once.
A paper moon turns over inside a closed wooden drawer.
The small girl shares her blue chalk and keeps the green piece.
A warm plate waits beside the folded cloth after breakfast.
One dry leaf circles the floor though the door stays shut.
Uncle listens beside the lamp until Leo reaches the end.
A hard gust lifts dust from the road before the first heavy drops.
The soft coat hangs near the cup in a patch of morning sun.
A glass bead feels warm although it rested in the dark cupboard.
A neighbour returns the red ball and asks Leo to keep it safe.
The little bed holds a smooth blanket under the pale window.
Thunder shakes the shelf while water runs beneath the fence.
Two children make a space between them and show Leo their map.
Fast drops cross the roof as the tall tree bends toward the wall.
A clean spoon rests by the warm cup on the wooden table.
The blue block stands upright after every other block has fallen.
Grandfather saves the last pear and cuts it into equal pieces.
Evening light reaches the pillow beside a freshly washed shirt.
Wet leaves race past the gate while the sky makes one deep sound.
A small bell moves without ringing and then rings while still.
Cold rain covers the steps as the gutter answers in quick beats.
The kitchen cloth is warm where the quiet kettle stood.
Two chalk marks meet beneath the chair although nobody drew them.
A cousin brings a book back and stays to hear Leo choose a page.
